ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is an inscribed quadrilateral of the circle $\odot O$, and $\angle BCD=120^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle BOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle BCD = 120^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle A = 180^\circ - \angle BCD = 60^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle BOD = 2\angle A = \boxed{120^\circ}$.

The line segments AB, BC, CD, DA form the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD. Point O is located inside the circle, labeled as the center of the circle, and the radii OB and OD are drawn, so ∠BOD is the central angle formed by the radii OB, OD. Reasoning: It is known that ∠BCD = 120°. Because ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary, so ∠BAD = 180° - 120° = 60°. ∠BAD is the inscribed angle subtending arc BD, while ∠BOD is the central angle subtending the same arc BD; therefore the central angle is equal to 2 times the inscribed angle, ∠BOD = 2 × 60° = 120°.
